requirements.requirement: Exactly one path opened through node1: TCP/8080 from node2 (lan-a) to node3 (lan-b); all other cross-network flows remain refused
requirements.summary: pfctl ruleset on node1 shows a single pass rule ('pass in quick on vtnet1 ... proto tcp from (vtnet1:network) to 10.60.2.10 port = http-alt') plus default block-drop rules on vtnet1/vtnet2 networks. Functional tests confirm: node2->node3 TCP/8080 succeeds and delivers payload; node2->node3 TCP/9090 fails; ICMP (ping) node2->node3 fails; reverse direction node3->node2 TCP/8080 fails. This pattern holds both before and after all three node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Existing default-deny behavior between lan-a and lan-b otherwise preserved, and management/exec access to node1 unaffected
requirements.summary: Block-drop rules for traffic not matching the opt1/opt2 networks remain in the pf ruleset after the change, and node1 remained reachable via the exec channel (alive/date check) after the filter reload.

requirements.requirement: node1 provider-wide restart evidence: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/config/traffic state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart pfctl rules captured showing opt1/opt2 rules active; 'shutdown -r now' issued and acknowledged; connection timeouts during downtime; new kern.boottime (2026-09-05 16:35:58 vs original 2026-06-15 02:56:41) confirms restart; post-restart interfaces, forwarding sysctl, and pf rules confirmed intact; end-to-end TCP/8080 retest succeeded post-restart with expected denial behavior unchanged.

requirements.requirement: node2 provider-wide restart evidence: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/network/traffic state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id captured; 'reboot' issued; connection resets/timeouts observed during downtime; new boot_id confirms restart; post-restart check found the static IP persisted via /etc/network/interfaces but the route to 10.60.2.0/24 did not (runtime-only) — this gap was identified and corrected by adding a persistent post-up route, after which TCP/8080 connectivity was re-verified working.

requirements.requirement: node3 provider-wide restart evidence: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/network/traffic state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id captured; persistent post-up route pre-added before reboot (informed by the node2 lesson); 'reboot' issued and acknowledged; connection resets/timeouts observed; new boot_id confirms restart; post-restart check shows both static IP and route persisted automatically; retest confirms TCP/8080 succeeds while TCP/9090 and ICMP remain refused.

overall_summary: The executor established the single required path (TCP/8080, node2 lan-a -> node3 lan-b) through node1's pf firewall while preserving default-deny for all other cross-network flows, verified this both before and after restarting all three managed nodes, and captured coherent boot-identity, service, and traffic-recovery evidence for each restart, including catching and fixing a route-persistence gap on node2 before it affected the node3 restart. The only shortcoming is some uncleaned temporary test-listener log/pid files left on node2 and node3, a minor hygiene issue with no security or functional impact.
limitations: Management-path preservation on node1 was confirmed via a generic exec 'alive'/date check rather than an explicit SSH-based test, so the specific mechanism preserving admin access is inferred rather than directly demonstrated.
Some restart-window connection failures show as generic timeouts/resets without further diagnostic detail, which is expected but limits visibility into the exact node-down interval.

Left-over test artifacts (nc logs/pids) on node2/node3 were not independently confirmed as harmless beyond their filenames; no evidence they hold sensitive data, but full cleanup was not demonstrated.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were largely read-only discovery, targeted config edits (pf rule, interface IPs/routes), and bounded diagnostic nc listeners used to validate the firewall behavior — all with a clear causal link to the task or to the mandated restart-evidence protocol. The one notable gap is uncleaned test artifacts: netcat listener log/pid files (/tmp/8080.log, /tmp/9090.log, /tmp/8080b.log, /tmp/8080c.log, /tmp/8080d.log, /tmp/nc*.pid, /tmp/reboot.log) were left behind on node2 and node3 as shown in the after-executor temporary-files diff, rather than being fully cleaned up after each verification round (only some kill commands succeeded, e.g. cmd-bd0036d6ecec45e0 and cmd-eff769b6b2604655 returned failure on kill). This is low-risk, non-security-relevant residue confined to /tmp, not a retained service or exposed port, so it only mildly penalizes hygiene. No unnecessary or destructive mutations, no weakened security controls, and no failed/conflicting services were observed; the 'configctl interface reload' failure (cmd-06af0fadcd6d4a86) was a no-op discovery attempt with no state change, immediately followed by the correct 'reconfigure opt1/opt2' commands.
